root_cause.text: An out-of-bounds memory read occurs because `parse_dacl()` assumes a SID that matches `sid_unix_NFS_mode` via `compare_sids()` always has at least three subauthorities, but `compare_sids()` only compares the minimum number of subauthorities, so a truncated SID with two subauthorities can match, and the subsequent access to `sid.sub_auth[2]` reads past the end of the ACE.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `ppace[i]->sid.num_subauth >= 3` before comparing the SID and reading `sub_auth[2]`. The commit description states: "That assumes the ACE carries three subauthorities, but compare_sids() only compares min(a, b) subauthorities. A malicious server can return an ACE with num_subauth = 2 and sub_auth[] = {88, 3}, which still matches sid_unix_NFS_mode and then drives the sub_auth[2] read four bytes past the end of the ACE."
